governanceModel: First EU member state with its own comprehensive national AI law

First-mover national AI law vs. EU harmonisation
overview:
Italy became the first EU member state to pass its own comprehensive national AI law, Law No. 132/2025, which entered into force in October 2025 and layers sector-specific rules — for healthcare, employment, justice and the professions — plus new AI copyright provisions on top of the EU AI Act baseline. Implementing decrees are due by October 2026; two received preliminary government approval in June 2026.

Undersecretary Alessio Butti frames the law as a 'digital sovereignty' matter, citing a €1 billion national investment. The law's copyright provisions are notably strict: AI-assisted works are protected only with genuine human creative contribution, and text-and-data-mining is permitted only for research or non-commercial use unless rights holders opt in — a tighter stance than most of the EU.

debates.topic: TDM copyright restriction scope contested by industry vs. rightsholders
debates.summary: Italy's national law permits text-and-data-mining for AI training only for research or non-commercial use unless rights holders opt in — stricter than the EU baseline and contested by industry.
debates.expanded: AI developers argue the research/non-commercial-only default makes Italy a harder jurisdiction to train commercial models in compared to peers relying solely on the EU AI Act's copyright framework. Rightsholders and creative-industry groups support the stricter default, arguing it better protects Italian creative and publishing industries.

debates.topic: First-mover national AI law vs. EU harmonisation
debates.summary: As the first EU state with its own comprehensive AI law, Italy tests whether national add-ons atop the AI Act help or fragment the single market.
debates.expanded: The European Commission has generally pushed for harmonised AI Act implementation across member states; Italy's decision to legislate additional sector-specific and copyright rules raises the question of whether other states will follow suit (creating a patchwork within the EU itself) or whether Brussels will push back on national divergence.
